# Hermes Agent: Onboarding & FAQ Guide

### 1. Installation & Platforms
- **Windows**: Tier 1 support via `install.ps1` without WSL2. WSL2 is only needed if using the embedded web dashboard `/chat` terminal (requires a POSIX PTY).
- **Docker / ARM64 / NAS**: Official multi-arch images (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. For NAS bind mounts (UGOS, Synology, unRAID), set `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) so the container remaps permissions to write `/opt/data`.
- **Android (Termux)**: Fully supported in `install.sh` and `hermes update`. Detects Termux, sets `ANDROID_API_LEVEL`, installs the curated `[termux-all]` dependency group, and routes temporary files to writable `$TMPDIR` instead of `/tmp`.
- **Web Dashboard**: Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI and chat interface at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`.
- **Slow Updates (`hermes update`)**: The Node.js update step may pause during Camofox postinstall while it silently downloads a browser binary without progress output.

### 2. Models & Providers
- **Small Local Models (Ollama/Qwen 4B–9B)**: Hermes passes ~45 tool schemas per turn. To reduce latency: disable unused tools (`hermes tools`), use faster quantizations, or set `terminal.backend: local` in `config.yaml`.
- **Local Endpoint Ignored**: If `provider: auto` picks up remote environment API keys, set `provider: custom` with `base_url: http://localhost:11434`.
- **Ollama Cloud**: Use the built-in `ollama-cloud` provider (routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`).
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Set `provider: azure-foundry` and export `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` (or configure via `hermes setup`).
- **Claude Pro/Max vs API**: API keys are always billed separately by Anthropic. To use Pro/Max subscription allowances, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Gemini**: Legacy CLI and Antigravity OAuth providers are removed. Use Google AI Studio API keys (`GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`).
- **DeepSeek V4 Charges**: `model_normalize.py` historically normalized `deepseek-v4-flash` to `deepseek-chat`, which the upstream API routed to the more expensive `deepseek-v4-pro`. Ensure model names pass through unnormalized.
- **Vision for Custom Models**: Set `supports_vision: true` under your model configuration.
- **Open WebUI Streaming**: Fixed signature mismatch in `_on_tool_progress` (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`); tool execution progress streams properly over SSE.
- **Token Usage on Local Providers**: Streaming OpenAI-compatible backends automatically receive `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` to capture token usage in `/usage`.
- **Model Routing Policy**: Complexity-based automatic model routing (`smart_model_routing`) is intentionally removed. Switch models manually (`/model`, `hermes chat -m <model>`) or configure `delegation.model` for subagents.

### 3. Gateways, Messaging & Personas
- **Gateway Setup Wizard**: Run `hermes gateway setup` to interactively configure Discord, Telegram, and other messaging platforms.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized user"**: `allowed_chats` filters group chats, not DM users. Authorize your user ID with `allow_from: "YOUR_ID"` (sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`), use pairing via `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `allow_all: true`.
- **File & Media Delivery**: Uploaded files (`.txt`, `.py`) are injected into context or cached. Outbound files and tool media are delivered natively across platforms: Matrix (`m.file`), Email attachments, Telegram images, and DingTalk (Markdown `![image](url)`).
- **MCP Image Handling**: Standard MCP base64 `ImageContent` results are automatically cached and converted into `MEDIA:<path>` tags for native platform media delivery.
- **Multi-Profile Gateways**: Multiplexed gateway mode runs secondary profile adapters (including WeChat/Weixin and Telegram) concurrently, keeping credentials, sessions, skills, and memory completely isolated per profile.
- **Per-Channel Personas & Delegation**: Set `channel_prompts` in platform configs for per-channel system prompts. Use `delegate_task` to spawn isolated subagent instances.

### 4. Memory, Context & Autonomy
- **Identity & Memory Files**:
  - `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Agent persona and instructions (seeded with a real default persona upon install).
  - `~/.hermes/USER.md`: Persistent user preferences and profile (`target="user"`, enabled by default).
  - `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md`: Long-term factual agent memory.
- **Local Honcho**: Local instances (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) no longer require an API key; Hermes accepts `base_url` alone and injects `"local"` placeholder credentials automatically. Upgrade via `hermes update`.
- **Custom Tools & Memory Plugins**: Built-in memory additions are closed. Install custom plugins into `~/.hermes/plugins/` and activate with `hermes plugins enable <name>`.
- **Context Management**: Built-in `ContextCompressor` automatically prunes and deduplicates verbose tool results before compaction. Custom engines can implement the `ContextEngine` ABC (`context.engine`).
- **Autonomous Goals & Turn Budgets**: Sessions enforce `agent.max_turns` (default 90). Use `/goal <task>` for persistent cross-turn execution (Ralph loop) and resume paused runs with `/goal resume`.
- **Session Resumption**: Crashed or interrupted sessions are marked `resume_pending` to preserve session ID and transcript. Automatic reset is disabled by default (`session_reset.mode: none`); restore previous sessions with `/resume`.

### 5. Diagnostics & Observability
- **Diagnostics**: Run `hermes doctor` to verify environment, auth tokens, and configuration.
- **Skill Telemetry**: Track skill executions via `/insights` or `hermes insights` (`~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).
- **Call Tracing**: Enable turn-level Langfuse tracing with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Security Reporting**: Report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by email to `security@nousresearch.com`.
